# Writing tools

::: {.doc-lead}
Adjust the reading surface, fix spelling with on-device suggestions, and manage technical vocabulary.
:::

Shortcuts are written with **Ctrl** and **Alt**; on macOS use **⌘** for Ctrl and **⌥** for Alt. [Keyboard shortcuts](/docs/shortcuts.html#paper) lists every Paper shortcut.

## Text size {#text-size}

The status bar carries a text-size slider on its own row, just above **Local**, **Export**, and
the word count. Drag it, use the **−** and **+** buttons beside it, or press **Ctrl+=** and **Ctrl+-** from
anywhere in Paper; **Ctrl+0** goes back to 100%. The range is 50% to 250%.

This changes the real type, not a zoom of the picture: the text redraws at the new size, the
lines re-wrap, and the column of text widens or narrows with them. Nothing about the document
on disk changes — text size is a reading preference for this device.

Click the percentage to choose **which panels** it applies to. The small window that opens has
a checkbox for **All panels together** and one each for the **Manuscript**, the **Left
sidebar**, and the **Right margin** — tick any one, any combination, or all three. By default
the slider resizes the manuscript only, so the sidebar and margin keep their size while you
make your text bigger. Each panel remembers its own size, and both the sizes and your choice
of panels come back the next time you open Flux. At least one panel always stays ticked.

## Local corrections {#local-corrections}

Paper fixes unmistakable typing slips as soon as you finish a word: transposed letters such as
*compelx* and an accidental space such as *o bject*. The replacement fades into place with a small
blue pulse beneath it, and the caret never moves. Anything less certain — a missing or extra
letter, a word with several plausible neighbours — is not guessed at: it is underlined for you to
decide (see [Spelling suggestions](#sentence-judgment)).

Checking runs in a local Harper worker and never sends manuscript text anywhere. Acronyms,
mixed-case scientific names, numbers, code, math, citations, links and table source are left
alone. Project titles, authors, references, figure captions and recurring technical terms feed the
local vocabulary.

| To | Do this |
|---|---|
| See what changed | Click the pulsed word. The popover shows *original → replacement*. |
| Take a correction back | **Undo** in the popover, or **Ctrl+Z**. Each correction is its own undo step, so word-by-word changes stay independently undoable. Undoing also teaches this project not to repeat that correction. |
| Keep the word for good | **Add to dictionary** in the popover stores it as project vocabulary. |
| Switch checking on or off | Click **Local** in the status bar (blue when the checker is ready), use **Settings → Corrections → Local corrections**, or the command palette. |

This layer does not rephrase, make stylistic edits or guess at the spelling of scientific
compounds; those are choices, not safe automatic corrections.

## Spelling suggestions {#sentence-judgment}

A word the checker cannot resolve is underlined in red.

1. **Hover** the word to see up to five ranked suggestions. The keyboard stays in the manuscript.
2. **Click** the word to put the keyboard in the list: **↑** and **↓** move, **Enter** picks,
   **Escape** closes. Start typing to write your own spelling in the box below the list, then
   press **Replace** (or **Enter**).
3. If the word is correct, press **+** in the popover to add it to your **Personal** dictionary.
   The underline disappears at once, including other occurrences in open documents.

<figure class="doc-figure doc-figure-compact"><a href="/assets/media/docs/paper-spelling.png" data-enlarge data-caption="Hover a red underline for ranked suggestions; + adds the word to your Personal dictionary."><img src="/assets/media/docs/paper-spelling.png" alt="A sentence in the Paper editor with a misspelled word underlined in red and a popover above it listing ranked spelling suggestions, with buttons to add the word to the dictionary or dismiss it." width="1240" height="660" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Hover a red underline for ranked suggestions; <strong>+</strong> adds the word to your Personal dictionary.</figcaption></figure>

Flux remembers the correction — picked from the list, typed in the box, or retyped by hand as one
of the suggestions — and applies it automatically the next time you type that misspelling
followed by a space or punctuation. The automatic correction gets the same blue pulse: **Ctrl+Z**
restores what you typed, and clicking it offers **Forget** to stop making that correction.
Learned corrections are remembered across projects.

Your Personal dictionary starts with common neuroscience and biology vocabulary (*interneuron*,
*GABAergic*, *parvalbumin*, *synaptogenesis* and many more), so those words are never flagged.
Remove a supplied term through [Word tools](#dictionaries); the removal stays in effect after
reopening Flux.

Opening an existing document scans its prose in the background and flags possible issues without
changing the text — a few hundred marks at most. The scan skips the sentence you are writing in,
along with code, math, tables, citations, links and front matter. Edit a flagged sentence and the
normal checking takes over.

## Dictionaries and aliases {#dictionaries}

Select one word — ordinary selection and Vim visual mode work the same — and click **Word tools**
(the small book in the floating toolbar), or press **Shift+Alt+W**. Add the word at either scope:

| Scope | Where it applies | Toggle without the dialog |
|---|---|---|
| **Project** | Only inside the current Flux project | **Shift+Alt+D** |
| **Personal** | Every Flux project on this device | **Alt+D** |

The buttons and shortcuts are true toggles: select the term again to remove it. Dictionary terms
are protected from ordinary corrections and become high-confidence targets for nearby mechanical
mistakes — after adding *iGluSnFR4f*, a typed *IgluSnrf4* can resolve to the canonical spelling.
Flux stays conservative around plausible scientific variants: a stored *SLAP2* does not turn
*SLAP3* into *SLAP2*.

**Aliases** expand a short form when you finish typing it. Select *iGluSnFR4f*, enter `igf`, choose
Project or Personal, and add it. The next time `igf` is typed as its own word, the delimiter
(space, punctuation or Return) morphs it into *iGluSnFR4f* with the same blue pulse. One **Ctrl+Z**
restores `igf`; clicking the pulsed expansion offers **Remove alias**, and every saved alias has
its own **×** in **Word tools**. Project aliases take priority over Personal aliases when both use
the same short form.

## Correction settings {#correction-settings}

**Settings → Corrections** holds the few choices the checker offers; see the
[Settings reference](/docs/settings.html#corrections) for the whole dialog.

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Local corrections** — *Correct clear typing and spacing errors as I write* | The on-device checker described above. The same switch is **Local** in the status bar. |
| **Reset correction learning** | Clears the automatic "leave alone" lessons taught by undoing corrections. Dictionaries and aliases are kept. |
| **English dialect** | **US**, **British**, **Canadian** or **Australian English** — which spellings count as correct. |

Everything in this section runs on your device.

## Vim, and how the caret feels {#vim-and-how-the-caret-feels}

For keyboard fans, **Ctrl+K → Enable Vim mode** turns on modal editing, with two flavours:
plain **Vim**, or **flux-ViM** — Vim plus Flux's opt-in refinements (the first: `jj` in insert
mode is Escape). If you do not use Vim, leave it off.

The caret glides after your typing: it arrives quickly and settles softly. Large jumps move
directly to the new position, and the caret blinks softly once you pause. There is nothing to
configure.
